message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in Monopoly.

I have a pink monopoly with hotels and $1711 cash. The opponent has $766 and owns the entire brown, light blue, and dark blue set. I am on North Carolina Avenue.

The opponent has mortgaged most of his properties. I am weighing whether to end the turn, propose a trade, unmortgage my railroads, or sell my pink hotels. I will likely keep my Get Out of Jail Free cards and avoid trading Tennessee Avenue.

I mapped the board positions from North Carolina. Rolling a 5 lands on Park Place with a $1,500 hotel rent. Rolling a 7 lands on Boardwalk with a $2,000 hotel rent. Both are heavily owned by the opponent.

I checked whether my cash covers the hotel rent on Park Place. It does, but Boardwalk is $289 short. I am verifying how much a pink hotel sells for to decide if selling one would bridge that gap.

I am checking the exact sellback value of a hotel. In standard Monopoly, a hotel sells for half its cost and reverts to four houses.

I realized a hotel on the pink properties costs $100, so selling it returns only $50. This contradicts my earlier assumption that one hotel sold for $250. I am now reconsidering whether to sell a hotel or simply sell houses.

Selling a hotel returns half its cost, and the four houses revert to the bank. That totals $250 per property, matching my earlier assumption. I can sell hotels separately from houses.

Selling one hotel returns only $50, which is far short of the $289 needed to cover Boardwalk. I am now calculating how many houses to sell from the remaining properties to make up the difference.

I calculated that selling one hotel plus five houses from another property yields $300, which covers the Boardwalk shortfall. I also noted that unmortgaging would cost cash rather than raise it.

I am now reconsidering whether to pre-sell buildings now. My previous strategy avoided pre-selling because the chance of landing on Boardwalk is only about 16.7 percent, and keeping full rent pressure on the opponent is preferable.

This is a post-turn decision, so the next roll has not happened yet. If I land on Boardwalk next turn, I will have an opportunity to sell buildings and pay rent during the standard debt resolution phase.

I will keep my buildings and only sell them if I land on Boardwalk. I can liquidate during the standard debt resolution phase.

I mapped the opponent's position on the Pennsylvania Railroad. Their next roll would land on St. James, a Community Chest, Tennessee Avenue, New York Avenue, Free Parking, Kentucky Avenue, and another Community Chest. Only Tennessee is mortgaged by me, so it would not generate rent.

The opponent's next roll would also land on Indiana, Illinois, B&O, Atlantic, and Ventnor, all of which are mortgaged by me. My pink properties sit behind them, so they will not hit those streets this turn. They recently built hotels on the brown set, which cost $500 total, leaving them with $766 cash.

The opponent's active rent threats against me are light blue hotels at $550 and $600, brown hotels at $250 and $450, and dark blue hotels at $1,500 and $2,000. I may hit a dark blue this roll before passing GO. After collecting $200 from GO, my cash would rise to about $1,911. I will keep my pink hotels intact as the only weapon to bankrupt the opponent.

The opponent can cover a pink hotel hit with cash alone. Virginia Avenue's $900 rent is only $134 short of their $766, so they could sell some brown or light blue buildings to pay it. This means one pink hit no longer forces a dark blue downgrade. Earlier assumptions that $966 cash made the pink rent payable are now in doubt.

A second pink hotel hit would be devastating. The opponent would need to strip light blue and brown buildings, and possibly dark blue hotels too.

The distance from the Pennsylvania Railroad to St. Charles Place is 36 spaces. That is nearly a full lap around the board.

I am considering trading my mortgaged Tennessee Avenue to the opponent. That would give them an orange monopoly, but they would need to unmortgage all three orange properties and build houses, which is expensive.

Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue costs $99, plus $99 for St. James and $110 for New York, leaving no room to build houses. An orange monopoly would be dangerous because I will pass through those streets after collecting GO. I will not trade Tennessee Avenue. The opponent cannot afford to break my dark blue hotels.

I cannot complete any color set through trade, so I will not trade cash or mortgaged properties. I will keep my two Get Out of Jail Free cards for flexibility. Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would cost 110 percent of its mortgage value.

Unmortgaging the Pennsylvania Railroad would cost $110 and yield only $25 in rent, so it is not worthwhile. Unmortgaging Tennessee Avenue would cost $99 and produce just base rent without completing a set. I will not sell my pink hotels because I am not in debt. I will end the turn.
